children: L&T Semiconductor Technologies showcases its first silicon carbide platform alongside an India-designed BLDC motor controller at Semicon India 2026
L&T Semiconductor Technologies (LTSCT), the semiconductor arm of Larsen & Toubro, has unveiled 40 products at Semicon India 2026, marking its entry into silicon carbide (SiC) products.

LTSCT has expanded its portfolio across power electronics, computing, connectivity, and secure identity applications. The showcase includes the company’s first 1,200V SiC MOSFET platform and a fully designed-in-India brushless DC (BLDC) motor controller.

The portfolio reflects LTSCT’s effort to move from semiconductor design towards scalable products and market-ready applications. The company is showcasing the products under the theme ‘Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem’, with applications spanning electric mobility, energy infrastructure, digital payments, surveillance and computing.

The 1,200V SiC MOSFET platform is designed for next-generation power conversion applications, including EV fast chargers, microgrids, solid-state transformers and traction inverters. LTSCT is also showcasing its first in-house silicon carbide power modules and devices as part of its power discrete and high-power portfolio.

Silicon carbide is used in power electronics where higher efficiency and performance are required, making the technology relevant to electric mobility and power infrastructure applications. LTSCT’s entry into SiC products therefore expands its semiconductor portfolio beyond conventional power devices into higher-voltage applications.

The company has also taped out a highly integrated BLDC motor controller that it says has been fully designed in India. The chip incorporates protection features and a flexible architecture intended to allow a single platform to support multiple models.

LTSCT said the architecture could help reduce bill-of-materials costs while supporting more energy-efficient BLDC ceiling fans. The product represents another step towards developing semiconductor products around specific applications rather than focusing only on chip design.

Beyond power electronics, LTSCT is showcasing an in-house designed USB-C gallium nitride (GaN) charger and a Vision Camera system-on-chip that combines image processing with on-device artificial intelligence acceleration. It is also displaying a Secure Identity Platform for applications including e-passports, payment cards and national identity systems, with hardware-rooted security and cryptographic acceleration.

In connectivity and radio frequency products, the company is showcasing four indigenously designed modules for smart metering, automotive applications and digital payments. These include an LCC43 Dynamic QR and Soundbox proof of concept for the National Payments Corporation of India’s proposed Trusted Device Layer.

The broader portfolio covers power, compute, analogue and mixed-signal products, Internet of Things modules and radio frequency technologies. LTSCT said the products target sectors including automotive, industrial, energy, data centres and telecommunications.

LTSCT Chief Executive Sandeep Kumar said the company is backing India’s semiconductor ambitions through investment, engineering capabilities and a focus on developing products for a self-reliant chip ecosystem.

The company said its Semicon India showcase aligns with the Semicon 2.0 initiative, which focuses on taking semiconductor designs from innovation to scalable products and market-ready solutions through greater ecosystem collaboration.
